title: deploy.sh follow-ups from #796's last review: trap wording and second signals, the --accept-live record and repeat, and owner-word wording
acceptance: scripts/deploy.sh's comment at the TERM/HUP traps and the self-check's name give the right reason: bash 3.2 runs the EXIT trap on SIGTERM/SIGHUP with $? set to the last command's status, so on_deploy_exit could skip the hint; the traps turn the signals into exits 143/129.

The failed-upload hint says "wrangler deploy failed or was interrupted (exit N); it may have uploaded. Run … wrangler deployments status." (a signal that reaches only bash while wrangler runs can fire before DEPLOY_UPLOADED=1).
on_deploy_exit starts with trap '' TERM HUP INT, so a second signal can't cut the hint and the worktree removal short.
--accept-live is recorded in the tag (DEPLOY_LIVE_NOTE) whenever it was passed and matched, including the no-tag and unknown-tag-Worker paths; a repeated --accept-live exits 2.

Every mention of --allow-batch and --accept-live (deploy.sh :10 and :24 comments, runbook :108 and :126, AGENTS.md's no-tag sentence, release-status.mjs :258 and :330) names both the owner's word in the session and HISTORY; runbook :156 says the rehearsal ask that names <previous-version-id> meets the 'owner has seen the live version' condition.

Optional, the record says which were done: N3 also lists what a diverged (not only an older) commit takes back; the live refusal omits an empty 'source:' line; the two long unwrapped lines in start-session.md and the runbook are wrapped; DEPLOY_ALLOW is kept only as the self-check's regression case.
